what_this_file_is: Every factual claim this project makes about its own sources is recorded here with the
exact URL, the retrieval date and the observation that supports it. Anything not listed
here is either an assumption (forbidden) or explicitly marked as an unverified lead.
This file is the anti-hallucination ledger: if a claim is not in here and not in a
record's `sources`, it must not appear on the website or in the README.

verified_facts.claim: The official HTML report family exists for season 20232024 with report kinds GS (Game Summary), ES (Event Summary), PL (Play-by-Play) and RO (Club Playing Roster).
observations: GS020001.HTM parsed: 8 goals, NSH 3 - TBL 5, footer '2024-02-06 11.19.44'
ES020001.HTM parsed: per-player G/A/P table, shots summary 3-31 / 5-34
PL020001.HTM parsed: chronological events with on-ice skaters
RO020001.HTM parsed: lineups, scratches, coaches, referees Rooney/Brenk, linespersons Alphonso/Brisebois

verified_facts.claim: There is no 'SC' report family. https://www.nhl.com/scores/htmlreports/20232024/SC020001.HTM returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-07.
The report index page https://www.nhl.com/scores/htmlreports/ returns HTTP 403 and cannot be used to enumerate seasons.

Official reports carry a generation timestamp in the document footer, and it distinguishes two eras: documents generated on game night (frozen originals) and documents regenerated long afterwards (current state).
observations: 2023-24 RO020001: footer '2024-02-06 11.20.12' -> same regeneration batch as the GS (28 seconds apart)
verified_facts.conclusion: Through at least 2016-17 the live document preserves the original game-night record; by 2023-24 documents are regenerated. The exact transition season is NOT established and must be measured by `python -m nhl_monitor probe` / the coverage job.

verified_facts.claim: Historic coverage of the official HTML report path is bounded: https://www.nhl.com/scores/htmlreports/19992000/GS020001.HTM returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-07, while 2005-06 documents are served normally.
verified_facts.conclusion: Earliest reliable season still to be established between 1999-2000 (absent) and 2005-06 (present) - the coverage job must probe each season folder.

GET /v1/gamecenter/2023020001/boxscore -> HTTP 200, NSH 3 - TBL 5, shots 31/34

verified_facts.claim: The JSON API and the HTML reports are the same official data rendered twice: player identifiers and the scoring record agree between them.
observations: Play-by-play goal event for 2023020001 goal #1 has scoringPlayerId=8476453, assist1PlayerId=8475167, assist2PlayerId=8478010, awayScore=0, homeScore=1 at 09:48 P1
Official Game Summary GS020001.HTM goal #1 reads '1 | 1 | 9:48 | EV | TBL | 86 N.KUCHEROV(1) | 77 V.HEDMAN(1) | 21 B.POINT(1)'
Independent id check from the Play-by-Play report text: 'NSH #2 SCHENN HIT TBL #86 KUCHEROV' pairs sweater 86 with 8476453
verified_facts.consequence: Disagreement between the two is therefore a real change signal, but the two sources are NOT independent - they must not be treated as two witnesses in the record's evidence.

verified_facts.claim: Negative control for the archive method: the archived copy of GS020001.HTM (20232024) taken 2025-01-25 shows the same scoring summary and the same document footer as the live document retrieved 2026-10-07.
observations: Wayback snapshot 20250125005135 (id_ raw) contains the identical eight-goal scoring summary and the same footer '2024-02-06 11.19.44'
Therefore no scoring change is detectable for that game from that pair of observations
verified_facts.consequence: The digest/diff method produced zero false positives on this control. It also proves that a document regeneration (footer change) is not by itself evidence of a scoring change - a content diff is required. And it demonstrates the reverse risk: a snapshot taken AFTER a correction cannot reveal it.

verified_facts.claim: The Wayback CDX index exposes a content digest per snapshot of an official document, which makes 'did this official document ever change?' an answerable question without downloading every version.
observations: Exact-URL query for 20232024/GS020001.HTM -> one row: statuscode 200, digest TE24NPUUMSEV3LQEBNQE2TN3NO5GNATJ, timestamp 20250125005135, length 4435
Prefix query for 20242025/ returned rows with digests, e.g. ES010026.HTM digest CBOFKLR7ECD2HM5O3K74TQ7RM5O7TEUM at 20250115055117

verified_facts.claim: Archive coverage is sparse and noisy and must be filtered before it can be used as evidence.
observations: The 2005-06 prefix sample contains 2006-era captures that are HTTP 302 redirects with digest 3I42H3S6NNFQ2MSVX7XZKYAYSCX5QBYJ (no body)

verified_facts.claim: Method validation for the frozen-era census (frozen official document vs current official database), sample size 1: they agree.
observations: Frozen GS020001.HTM (2005-10-05, MTL 2 - BOS 1) credits J. BULIS, P. BERGERON and M. RYDER with the goals

verified_facts.claim: The earliest season for which the official report host serves a game report is 2000-01; 1999-2000 returns HTTP 404.
verified_facts.method: Direct retrieval of the season's first game summary for several seasons.
observations: 19992000/GS020001.HTM -> '404 Not Found' (page title), no content
20002001/GS020001.HTM -> COL 2 - DAL 2, Wednesday October 4 2000, Reunion Arena, attendance 17,001, footer 2000-10-04-22.14.20
20012002/GS020001.HTM -> OTT 5 - TOR 4, Wednesday October 3 2001, Air Canada Centre, attendance 19,173, footer 2001-10-03-22.27.18
Both parseable reports carry footers within about 1 hour of the game, so they are FROZEN at game time and are the original record, not a later rebuild
verified_facts.consequence: A frozen report is what makes a historical correction detectable: the frozen document is the ORIGINAL record, so it can be diffed against the current official database for any season from 2000-01 onward.

verified_facts.claim: Official reports are either frozen at game time or regenerated in batches, and the two behaviours are distinguishable from the document footer alone.
verified_facts.method: Compare each report's footer timestamp with its game date.
observations: The regenerated 20242025 reports carry the post-correction credit, so a regenerated report is the CURRENT record
The NHL does not document the timezone of the footer, so footer times are stored verbatim and never converted into UTC

verified_facts.claim: The 2000-2004 Game Summary layout differs from the modern one in ways the parser must handle: the on-ice skaters of both teams are columns inside the SCORING SUMMARY, the strength column is last, and the header carries no league-shield logo.
verified_facts.method: Parse the fetched 2000-01 and 2001-02 reports and compare column order with the modern report.
observations: Header row: G | Per | Time | Team | Goal Scorer | Assist | Assist | <AWAY> | <HOME> | STR
Modern header for comparison: G | Per | Time | Str | Team | Goal Scorer | Assist | Assist | <AWAY> on Ice | <HOME> on Ice
Team logo images in this era are only the two club logos (logoccol.gif, logocdal.gif); the modern report also embeds logocnhl.gif, which is a league shield and not a team
Bench penalties appear with the literal player cell 'Team' and must not become players
The parser's ordering of goals by clock is now by SECONDS: as text, '18:31' sorted before '2:00' and the period came out in the wrong order

verified_facts.claim: The NHL publishes its scoring changes in a fixed, machine-parseable form on its own public-relations channel, and each announcement resolves to a specific goal in an official report.
verified_facts.method: Retrieve three announcement posts directly, parse them with nhl_monitor.ingest.parse_scoring_change_statement, and match each against the official Game Summary row for that goal.
observations: Format: 'OFFICIAL SCORING CHANGE: Game <n> @<away> at @<home> Goal at <M:SS> of the <ordinal> period now reads <scorer> from <assist1> and <assist2>. #NHLStats'
2025-03-27T04:51:19Z Game 1,140 NJD at CHI 6:50 P1 now reads Dawson Mercer from Luke Hughes and Nico Hischier -> GS021140.HTM goal 2: 91 D.MERCER(16) | 43 L.HUGHES(31) | 13 N.HISCHIER(28)
2025-04-09T04:50:32Z Game 1238 BOS at NJD 9:38 P1 now reads David Pastrnak from Morgan Geekie -> GS021238.HTM goal 1: 88 D.PASTRNAK(41) | 39 M.GEEKIE(23)
2025-04-02T05:07:35Z Game 1185 NSH at CBJ 9:02 P3 now reads Jordan Oesterle from Cole Smith and Michael McCarron -> GS021185.HTM goal 12: 82 J.OESTERLE(2) | 36 C.SMITH(8) | 47 M.MCCARRON(9)
All three announcements were posted between 2h49m and 3h25m after the reported end of the game, i.e. after the game had been published as final
All three change player credit only: the number of goals in each game is unchanged

verified_facts.claim: An official GameCenter payload can contain media metadata that still shows the SUPERSEDED credit of a goal, so the payload is not internally consistent after a correction.
verified_facts.method: Read the highlight-clip fields of the goal event that announcement A corrected.
observations: Event 146 of game 2024021140 (the corrected goal) carries highlightClipSharingUrl 'https://nhl.com/video/njd-chi-meier-scores-ppg-against-spencer-knight-6370610304112' (English, superseded name) and highlightClipSharingUrlFr 'https://nhl.com/fr/video/njd-chi-mercer-marque-un-but-en-a-n-contre-spencer-knight-6370608420112' (French, corrected name)
The scoring fields of the same event carry the corrected credit
A clip title is media metadata and NOT a scoring record; it is stored as corroboration of the superseded credit and flagged as an inconsistency inside an official payload

verified_facts.claim: The archive reaches the earliest season the league still serves (2000-01) but only from 2012 onward, and multi-version documents provably exist there: GS020011.HTM was captured six times with one digest, then twice with two different digests, then once with the original digest again.
verified_facts.method: CDX prefix query for nhl.com/scores/htmlreports/20002001/ (fl=original,timestamp,digest,statuscode, limit 250), retrieved 2026-10-07.
observations: GS020001.HTM captured 20130701044936 (digest MO7NXQMG3VXPD7BKEDRGLCC4KBBZPLXZ, status 200) and 20151029204855 (same digest, status '-'); the earliest capture is therefore 12 years after the game.

GS020011.HTM digest WOHA5LSRQQMSLIZ6XG7J425V7U3DTIT6 at 20171216213444, 20180126115413, 20180227204714, 20180402182325, 20180505024141, 20180609114015; then CFXV6R2S2EFF45DNCE6IKH6UJY6VHMZY at 20180711001821; then W35O3AYLKZPUR3VTB2ASHLD65HCX5ZU7 at 20180811025827; then back to WOHA5LSRQQMSLIZ6XG7J425V7U3DTIT6 at 20180812121249.

A digest that returns to an earlier value is therefore not hypothetical: it is observed on a real official document, which is why archive.change_windows() flags it instead of folding it into a change.
Captures exist under both http://www.nhl.com:80/ and http://www.nhl.com/ for the same document path.
consequence: No correction that happened before a document's first capture can be recovered from that capture - for 2000-01 that is a 12-year blind spot at the start of the documented era.
The archive cannot decide whether a digest change is a scoring correction or a capture artefact; only the content comparison can, which is what backfill.compare_captures() does.

verified_facts.claim: Archived multi-version documents also exist in the frozen era: the 2005-06 Event Summary ES020024.HTM was captured three times with digest SHZQVKE2D54SBOLEHCFFGWRZI6I7S7WX and then once with digest 5UD7G2PSUTPLYTVHJXTMJZTAOJOVEMDF, i.e. the document changed between 20101203140908 and 20150924103644.
verified_facts.method: CDX prefix query for nhl.com/scores/htmlreports/20052006/ (same fields), retrieved 2026-10-07.
observations: ES020024.HTM: SHZQVKE2D54SBOLEHCFFGWRZI6I7S7WX at 20101119084040, 20101126124951, 20101203140908; 5UD7G2PSUTPLYTVHJXTMJZTAOJOVEMDF at 20150924103644.

The same prefix contains 302 redirects from nhl.com:80 with digest 3I42H3S6NNFQ2MSVX7XZKYAYSCX5QBYJ and http:// captures of images with digest OQ3OBNFR7DBCFQ4ANGEQW5P2FOXZZJRA at status 301, confirming that both must be filtered out.

ES020007.HTM is archived under both http://www.nhl.com/ (digest ERE2FJ77DE6CMRDW4XIEFB3LGYBYFVEG) and https://www.nhl.com/ (digest TOEDQAVC47Q32YXANRZR3MEELO24AILK) - different document URLs, so those two captures are not compared with each other.
verified_facts.consequence: Report kinds other than the Game Summary can also be proven to have changed, but only the Game Summary carries the scoring record in a form the record builder can attribute to a goal, so backfill.COMPARABLE_KINDS deliberately lists GS only.

verified_facts.claim: A capture's URL does not identify the document: the archive holds the same 2000-01 document under http://www.nhl.com:80/..., http://www.nhl.com/... and https://www.nhl.com/.... Matching captures on the whole URL string discards real captures and undercounts how often a document was archived.
verified_facts.method: Observed in the two prefix queries above, then reproduced as a unit test on the parser (tests/test_archive_change.py, UrlVariantTests).
verified_facts.consequence: archive.parse_cdx() now matches captures on the document path (scheme, host and port ignored) while still excluding other documents in the same folder; each capture keeps its own original URL as evidence and records a flag when it differs from the canonical URL.

verified_facts.claim: The official play-by-play marks video reviews and coach's challenges as typeDescKey 'stoppage' with details.reason / secondaryReason values 'video-review' and 'chlg-<bench>-<type>'.
observations: 2026020033 (CGY@VAN 2026-10-03): eventId 508 P3 01:28 stoppage reason=video-review secondaryReason=video-review; goal eventId 822 at the same clock (Ohgren)
2026020015 (EDM@VAN 2026-10-01): eventId 43 P3 04:43 stoppage reason=referee-or-linesman secondaryReason=video-review; goal eventId 899 at the same clock (Rossi)
2026020044 (NSH@TOR 2026-10-06): eventId 454 P3 11:46 stoppage reason=chlg-vis-off-side; eventId 471 offside; NO goal event at 11:49 (the overturned Nylander goal is absent from the final record)
2016020214 (NYI@FLA 2016-11-12): eventId 292 P2 14:53 stoppage reason=chlg-vis-goal-interference; no goal event at 14:53
verified_facts.consequence: A review is detectable from the play-by-play (prefix chlg- or value video-review). A goal disallowed on review is REMOVED from the final play-by-play, so the stoppage plus the Situation Room statement are the only official evidence that it was ever signalled.

verified_facts.claim: The NHL publishes an official statement for every coach's challenge and Situation Room video review, as stories tagged 'situation-room' on its content API, continuously since February 2016.
verified_facts.method: Paginated https://forge-dapi.d3.nhle.com/v2/content/en-us/stories?tags.slug=situation-room&$limit=N&$skip=M on 2026-10-07 and read individual stories.
observations: $skip=0 newest item: VGK@SEA coach's challenge for game 2026020051 (contentDate 2026-10-07T02:40:24Z)

Each story: headline 'Coach's Challenge|Video Review: AWY @ HOM - M:SS of the Nth Period', markdown body with Result / Explanation (2019+ structured; 2016-18 prose + fields.description verdict), tags gameid-<10 digits> (most) and teamid-N; public page https://www.nhl.com/news/<slug>
Latency: CGY@VAN statement contentDate 2026-10-04T04:36Z for a play in the third period of a 10:00PM ET game (minutes); EDM@VAN statement 04:34Z for a 4:43-of-the-third play (about 20 minutes)
Some statements lack the gameid tag (e.g. edmonton-oilers-vancouver-canucks-video-review-x7720) and are resolved through the daily scoreboard
verified_facts.consequence: Goal <-> no-goal reversals caused by review are covered from the league's own words from 2016-02 onward (pipeline/nhl_scoring/situation_room.py). This is NOT a corrections feed for scorer/assist changes; none exists.

verified_facts.claim: GitHub Actions cron schedules on this repository are throttled far below the requested cadence.
verified_facts.method: gh run list --limit 100 filtered by event=schedule on 2026-10-07.
observations: monitor.yml requests '*/5 * * * *'; exactly one scheduled run (scoring monitor, 2026-10-07T11:50:52Z) appeared in more than eleven hours
verified_facts.consequence: Published cadence claims ('every 5 minutes', 'every 30 minutes') are not true in practice. Minutes-level alerting needs an external trigger (workflow_dispatch from another scheduler) or a self-hosted runner.
